summary: PhD chemist/materials scientist with 6+ years in optical/materials characterization, thin-film process development, DOE/SPC, and failure analysis. Builds reliable measurement workflows using spectroscopy, ellipsometry, thermal analysis, electrochemistry, and structured data to connect material signatures with process improvements.

bullets: Lead DOE-guided process-development experiments for bio-based polymer systems, defining material-quality readouts, process windows, reproducibility criteria, and scale-up specifications.
Translate FT-IR, thermal-analysis, spectroscopy, and process data into SOP-ready procedures and technical recommendations for repeatable execution.
Assessed reliability and degradation failure modes across 15+ functional material variants using spectroscopy, electrochemistry, thermal analysis, NMR/GPC, and MS-informed characterization.
Built process-property datasets connecting purity, stability, optical response, and performance to experimental conditions, anomalous results, and material-design recommendations.

Co-led AFOSR-funded molecular thin-film coating process development, optimizing CVD/surface-preparation conditions to improve reproducibility, morphology, interface quality, and optical/material performance.
Developed polymer thin-film deposition under flow using DOE strategies and in-situ QCM-D monitoring to quantify growth kinetics and coating reproducibility.

Managed characterization/process-development lab operations for a 15-member group; implemented calibration, SOP, safety, and equipment-tracking systems that improved instrument uptime by 30% and strengthened data quality.
